target.name: Tieton Farm & Creamery
target.classification: local farmstead creamery and diversified farm
target.distress_caveat: Do not infer insolvency, imminent failure, payroll distress, debt distress, or a desire for outside intervention from public evidence.

objective: Determine whether Tieton Farm & Creamery is a defensible first Evercraft Recovery target and, if so, identify the single best 14-day proof-of-revenue wedge to discuss with the operators before any external outreach or action.

public_facts.fact: Tieton Farm & Creamery describes itself as a small solar-powered farmstead creamery using milk from its own goats and sheep and also raising other pastured animals.

Its current Find Us page lists an on-farm seasonal stand Saturdays 11am-2pm through the end of October, Downtown Yakima Farmers Market Sundays through the end of October, Richland Farmers Market on alternating Fridays, Seattle-area retail/market outlets, and restaurant/tasting-room placements.

Its current cheese catalog includes Black Pearl, Venus, Bianca, Calypso, Sonnet, Ember, Phoebe, Rheba, Velvet, and Monalisa, with Rheba and Ember carrying past People's Choice awards described on the farm's site.

On August 31, 2026, NBC Right Now reported Lori Babcock publicly objected to a Yakima vendor permit increase from $118 to $325.50 and said she did not make $325 in one market and that many farmers-market vendors were struggling to make a living.

hypotheses_not_facts: The main recoverable bottleneck may be distribution, repeat purchasing, customer capture, or sales-channel mix rather than product quality.
Farmers markets may be functioning mainly as low-throughput transaction points when they could also acquire repeat customers.
A subscription/cheese-club offer could help only if contribution margin, inventory, production capacity, fulfillment load, and customer demand support it.
Holiday/corporate gifting could outperform subscriptions if inventory and Q4 demand support larger discrete orders.
Wholesale expansion could outperform direct-to-consumer offers if repeatable SKUs, margin, cold-chain/fulfillment capacity, and buyer demand support it.

proposed_pilot.positioning: No-retainer 14-day recovery pilot focused on attributable, collected net-new contribution rather than generic consulting deliverables.
proposed_pilot.founder_offer_under_review: If Evercraft cannot create measurable new collected sales attributable to the pilot, the operator owes no performance fee.
proposed_pilot.provisional_compensation: Approximately 15% of attributable collected net-new revenue during the pilot, subject to margin review and a dispute-resistant attribution rule.
baseline_before_action: Existing customer/contact capture and repeat-purchase rate where known
Fulfillment, shipping, refrigeration, food-safety, tax, and labor constraints
candidate_wedges: Focused wholesale expansion with 2-3 repeatable SKUs
Farm-stand/market customer capture into repeat purchasing
proposed_pilot.market_reframe_under_review: Treat markets as both sales channels and customer-acquisition surfaces only if the economics and operator workflow support it.

review_questions: Verdict: GO, GO WITH CHANGES, HOLD, or NO-GO on Tieton as Evercraft Recovery Case Study #001.
What is strongest in the proposed plan?
What is naive, dangerous, premature, commercially weak, or operationally unrealistic?
What must be learned before the first operator conversation, and what can only be learned from the operators?
Choose exactly ONE revenue wedge to test first, or say HOLD if choosing a wedge before baseline data would be irresponsible.
Define the correct 14-day success metric. Prefer collected contribution or another economically defensible measure over vanity revenue.
Is approximately 15% of attributable collected net-new revenue sensible? If not, propose a better structure.
Define a dispute-resistant attribution rule that protects both Tieton and Evercraft.
How could Evercraft accidentally create more cost, complexity, fulfillment burden, brand risk, or margin destruction than value?
Define the exact objective of the first 20-minute operator conversation and the three questions that matter most.
Challenge the target itself. Is Tieton actually a good first Recovery case, or does public evidence remain too thin?
guardrails: No spend, purchase, payment, contract, or obligation.
No claim that Tieton is insolvent, failing, desperate, or seeking Evercraft help.
Revenue without contribution margin can destroy value.
Production and fulfillment capacity are hard constraints.
Do not bury the operator in Evercraft software.
Respect food-safety, tax, shipping, labeling, refrigeration, and fulfillment realities.
